recipes.name: Easy Taco Rolls
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (15.25 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained
0.5 (8.75 ounce) can no-salt-added whole-kernel corn, drained

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).

Stir the rice and 1/2 cup water together in a microwave-safe bowl. Cover, and cook in the microwave on High for 6 minutes until the water is fully absorbed; set aside. While the rice is cooking, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in the ground beef. Cook and stir until the beef is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease.

Reduce heat to medium, and stir in the taco seasoning, corn, 1/2 cup water, 1 1/2 cups Cheddar cheese, and the cooked rice. Cook and stir until the cheese has melted and the corn is hot. Spoon the mixture into the flour tortillas. Roll into a tight cylinder, and pack into an 8x11-inch baking dish (it will be a tight squeeze). Pour the salsa over top, and sprinkle evenly with 1 1/2 cups Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until the cheese topping has melted and is beginning to brown, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Taco Rolls
raw_recipe.description: A taco meat mixture is rolled up into flour tortillas and baked in the oven for a few minutes for a quick and easy meal.

review.reviewBody: This was very good. I only substituted the minute rice with cooked brown rice and it was delicious. My family all had seconds and there was no leftover.

Too much sodium & MSG in packaged taco seasoning for us. I left out package of taco seasoning and used 2 kinds of chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, Mexican oregano, cayenne(just a little) to taste instead. threw some chopped onion and garlic in with Xlean beef and used Frozen corn, reduced sodium pintos(extra protein) then added no sodium beef stock to mixture to skillet instead of water. Used shredded Mexican cheese instead of cheddar--we like it better on TexMex/Mexican foods. I Sliced up an avocado, chopped a tomato, put out some sour cream, hot sauce and more salsa to be added to taste. Dish is plenty for us to have leftovers & they were even better.

Great for using up leftovers! I had leftover taco meat and some rice so I looked through the site for ideas and came across this recipe. It worked great and the potential for modifications are endless. I Heated up the meat and rice in a skillet and tossed in the other leftover items, cheese, onion, tomato, etc. Warmed the tortillas in the microwave, filled with heated mix then topped with salsa and cheese. Baked at 350 for 20 min until warm. Soooo tasty, quick and easy!

I LOVE this recipe!! I too wanted a good alternative to plain tacos and this is definitely it! I made a few changes, including adding onions to the ground beef while cooking, I also added about a half cup of salsa and 2 spoonfulls of sourcream to the meat mixture before putting it in the tortillas. I also used only half of the suggested corn amount out of personal preference. My fiance absolutely loved it and since it was just us two, there were lots of leftovers!

I cooked my meat with onions and garlic and followed the rest of the recipe... tasted the mix before filling my tortillas. I then decided it was missing some flavour... added 1/2 of the salsa jar to the mix... added a can of refried beans, 1 tbs of Chili powder and would have added some jalapeno but didn't have any. Next time, I'll use medium salsa instead of mild. This recipe is a good base but to me, it needed a little more punch to it.

I've made these twice and they are DELICOUS! I absolutely love this recipe, definitely a keeper. My boyfriend loved them, and we had lots of leftovers. Like the poster before me, I also used frozen corn instead of canned to reduce sodium. I also replaced the ground beef with ground turkey to reduce fat. I've made them twice: the first time with uncooked instant white rice and the next time with some mexican rice I'd made the day before and both were delicious. Next time I may try to throw in some black beans and maybe some chopped onion-- like another posted suggested, there really is so much that you can add/change to this and it'll probably still work! Thank you for posting this =]

this was so easy to make. i followed most of the recipe but added a few things. instead of using corn i used a can of diced tomato and green pepper. this gave it some kick. i sauteed diced onion in the hamburger. when putting together the tacos i lined the inside with lowfat refried beans. then put the filling in an rolled them up. this was perfect the family loved it! thanks for sharing.

I'm sure they would have been great as the recipe was written, but I didn't have minute rice so I quickly sauteed garlic, added some cumin and onion pwdr and Cavendars Greek Seasoning- browned rice in olive oil and added a can of stewed tomatoes and water to make the Spanish rice. I didn't have taco seasoning so I just used some of the above seasonings, ground beef and re-fried beans, corn & diced green chilies; Rolled both up in tortillas and mixed sour cream and salsa together to spread on top and topped with cheese. Then baked as directed.

This was pretty much perfect! I try many recipes and they're not all hits but this one definitely was. My VERY PICKY husband LOVED it and it will be come a regular in our household. 

I made a few changes: no corn (personal choice,) added 1/2 can black beans, 1/2 cup salsa & 2 spoonfuls of Sour Cream to the meat mixture before wrapping in the tortillas.

Highly recommend this EASY & delish dish!

Very good and easy. I added black bean to the mixture. Also, I smeared about a tablespoon of sour cream inside the middle of the tortilla then sprinkled with some chopped green onion before adding the mixture. Will be making this again!

Very good and easy. I added black bean to the mixture. Also, I smeared about a tablespoon of sour cream inside the middle of the tortilla then sprinkled with some chopped green onion before adding the mixture. Will be making this again!

Very easy and tasty. Used corn and rinsed black beans. Next time will add some jalapeno peppers for extra kick. Put the taco bar out so we could top with our favorite toppings (black olives, lettuce, sour cream, etc.) Thanks for the super easy recipe!
Really delicious and flexible! The only change I made was to add 1/2 of an onion, chopped. Can add black olives, black beans, green peppers, etc. Will absolutely make again.
"Meh" was our overall reaction. It seems like an extra hassle for not that much of an improvement. We decided to stick to the classic Taco Tuesday.

This was a good recipe to use up things in the fridge. I put the end bags of a couple of different cheeses and I used 1/2 jar salsa in the burger that I had in fridge. A bag of my frozen corn went in and I put in sriracha chili sauce, little more then a tbl to zip it up, along with taco mix from a bag. Topped it with mild enchilada sauce but next time I'll use salsa. Next time I want to add a little sour cream to burger mixture too. This is a keeper!
That was a wonderful meal. I like the way all the flavors came together. And it's so simple to make. Thank you!
I loved these! I added my own little touches and added black beans as well to the mixture. So yummy! This is has been added to my rotation of meals.
they were very good. will make them again
This was ok, flavor-wise, but the flour tortillas became gummy.
These are a hit! Easy to make! I used all regualar corn. Made a double batch, freezed two to a pack and used them in my husband's lunch.
